skill.description: Guides React 19 development with Actions, Server Components, modern hooks, secure server boundaries, and structured migration workflows.

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, JavaScript template literals, identifiers, and explicitly labeled security examples. Two migration steps invoke unpinned npx packages through @latest, creating a supply-chain execution risk. Separate examples omit object-level authorization and allow unverified uploads into a public directory; no prompt injection was found.

remediation.issue: Migration commands execute packages selected by the moving @latest tag.
remediation.suggestion: Pin each codemod to a reviewed exact version and require user confirmation before npx downloads or executes package code.

remediation.issue: The deleteUser security example authenticates users but does not authorize the target user ID.
remediation.suggestion: Verify that the caller owns the target account or has an explicit administrator role before deletion.

remediation.issue: The avatar example publishes unverified user-controlled file content.
remediation.suggestion: Allowlist media types, inspect file signatures, generate server-side names and extensions, scan content, and serve uploads from isolated storage.

semantic_findings.title: Missing Object-Level Authorization in Security Example
semantic_findings.description: The recommended deleteUser action authenticates the caller but deletes the supplied user ID without checking ownership or administrator permission. Copying this pattern permits an authenticated user to delete another user.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The action accepts an arbitrary ID and reaches the delete operation after only a non-null user check. The same skill security guide demonstrates the missing ownership or administrator check.

semantic_findings.title: Unrestricted File Content Written to a Public Directory
semantic_findings.description: The production upload example checks only file size, derives an extension from the client filename, and writes unverified content under public/uploads. This can enable malicious content hosting or stored browser attacks.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example performs a public write after a size check with no MIME allowlist, signature validation, content scanning, or safe server-generated extension. Its own security guide states that file type validation is required.

content.value_statement: React 19 introduces new async patterns and migration requirements. This skill guides implementation with Actions, Server Components, hooks, security practices, and upgrade examples.
actual_capabilities: Explains React 19 Actions, Server Components, Suspense, and execution boundaries.
Builds form workflows with useActionState, validation, pending states, and error feedback.
Designs optimistic interactions with useOptimistic and reconciliation after server responses.
Plans React 18 migrations using dependency updates, codemods, manual changes, tests, and rollback steps.
Reviews server actions for authentication, authorization, input validation, secret handling, and data exposure.
Provides complete reference examples for uploads, comments, dashboards, and progressive search.
limitations: The skill provides guidance and examples but does not execute, compile, or test an application.
Framework behavior differs between Next.js, Vite, and other React environments.
Package versions and vulnerability guidance require verification against current official advisories.
Production examples still require application-specific authorization, storage, validation, and observability decisions.

use_cases.title: Build a New React 19 Feature
use_cases.description: Create forms, optimistic updates, streaming views, or server actions with suitable React 19 patterns.

use_cases.title: Plan a React 18 Upgrade
use_cases.description: Identify breaking changes, sequence codemods, define validation tests, and prepare a rollback plan.

use_cases.title: Review Full-Stack React Boundaries
use_cases.description: Assess server actions, client components, secrets, authorization, input handling, and data exposure.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a React 19 Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain [React 19 feature] for a developer new to React 19. Include when to use it, key constraints, and a small example.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Action Form
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a React 19 form for [workflow] using useActionState. Include validation, pending feedback, error handling, and progressive enhancement.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a React 18 Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [project details] and produce a staged React 18 to React 19 migration plan with codemods, manual changes, tests, and rollback steps.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Full-Stack Pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [React 19 implementation] for server and client boundaries, authorization, secret handling, input validation, optimistic rollback, and deployment risks.

output_examples.input: Explain when to use useOptimistic for a comment form.
output_examples.output: Use optimistic state for immediate feedback, mark temporary comments clearly, reconcile server results, and restore confirmed state after failures.

output_examples.input: Plan a React 18 to React 19 migration for a TypeScript application.
output_examples.output: Upgrade through React 18.3, pin React 19 dependencies, run reviewed codemods, fix ref and type changes, test production builds, and document rollback.

output_examples.input: Review a server action that deletes an account by ID.
output_examples.output: Require authentication, verify ownership or administrator permission, validate the ID, handle missing records, record the action, and test unauthorized requests.

best_practices: Treat every server action as a public endpoint and enforce authentication, authorization, and validation.
Pin dependencies and codemods, review changes, and run tests before production deployment.
Keep secrets and server-only modules behind clear boundaries and pass minimal data to client components.
anti_patterns: Do not rely on client controls or hidden buttons as authorization.
Do not publish user uploads after checking only filename and size.
Do not execute moving package tags or migration tools without review and confirmation.

faq.question: Does this skill require Next.js?
faq.answer: No. Many examples use Next.js server features, but hook and migration guidance also applies to other React 19 environments.

faq.question: Can it migrate an application automatically?
faq.answer: No. It can plan changes and guide codemods, but the application still needs review, execution, and testing.

faq.question: Which React 19 hooks are covered?
faq.answer: It covers useActionState, useOptimistic, use, useTransition, useFormStatus, and related async interface patterns.

faq.question: Does it cover Server Components and Server Actions?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains execution boundaries, data access, forms, streaming, authentication, authorization, and secret handling.

faq.question: Are the package versions always current?
faq.answer: No. Verify versions and security advisories against official React and framework documentation before installation.

faq.question: Does the skill replace application security review?
faq.answer: No. Production systems need threat modeling, dependency review, access-control testing, secure upload design, and deployment-specific controls.
